content:
Alex Carter: Quick follow-up: here's a concrete playbook for "hot-layer" partial calibration to get safe, fast profiles for new model variants without full calibrations. Outline below.
Priya Sharma: sounds useful. what's the selection heuristic for 'hot' layers?
Mateo Ruiz: pick layers with highest activation variance and first/last N layers. Also include attention projection heads and layernorms.
Casey Li: we should represent sensitivity per-op (LN-eps, gelu variant, softmax temp) in a compact fingerprint so remaps are aware.
Lana Gomez: ops question: partial calib jobs must be limited resource-wise. propose org-level quota and per-host throttles.
Jing Wu: privacy: only send aggregated histograms (log-buckets) and hash of layer names. No raw activations.
Alex Carter: playbook steps: 1) collect activation histograms (anonymized) for 24h or N tokens; 2) compute sensitivity scores per-layer; 3) select top-K hot layers + boundary layers; 4) run targeted mixed-precision calib on hot set; 5) synth validation across buckets; 6) gated rollout.
Priya Sharma: validation should include both perf (latency/cost) and quality with delta thresholds per-bucket. Add a small human review gate for borderline results.
Mateo Ruiz: experiment idea: compare full-calib vs hot-layer calib on 3 models, track delta-accuracy + cost/time to generate. Expect large win in calibration time.
Casey Li: controller changes: add `partial_profile:true` and `hot_layers:[...]` fields, plus `max_layer_scale_change` guard.
Lana Gomez: ops-bot: please add a sampling guard and dashboard template for hot-layer calib.
ops-bot: ack. will create sampling-leaky-bucket and dashboard hotcalib/<id> with token-rate, job-cpu, and regression delta panels.
Jing Wu: I'll draft the histogram schema and privacy checklist.
Alex Carter: owners: Priya (policy + thresholds), Mateo (experiment notebooks), Casey (controller + schema), Lana (ops + dashboard), Jing (privacy). I'll file the RFC follow-up and assign tasks. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
